title: Comparison map for a closed factorization
statement:
Let $T,Z,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $g\colon T\to Y$, and suppose a factorization $g=z\circ h$ is supplied, where $h\colon T\to Z$ and $z\colon Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $g_{\mathrm{im}}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(g)\hookrightarrow Y$ for the scheme-theoretic image inclusion [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Define the comparison morphism
$$
c_{g,Z}\colon\operatorname{SIm}(g)\longrightarrow Z
$$
to be the closed-immersion lift of $g_{\mathrm{im}}$ through $z$, induced by the containment $\ker(z)\subseteq\ker(g)=\ker(g_{\mathrm{im}})$ of quasi-coherent kernel ideals. Thus the defining Mathlib expression is `IsClosedImmersion.lift z g.imageι H`, where $H$ is this containment. Here $\ker(g)$ is the largest quasi-coherent ideal contained in $\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to g_*\mathcal O_T)$, precisely as stated in the current [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. The image inclusion is the closed subscheme inclusion defined by that ideal; no quasi-compactness assumption on $g$ is imposed.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: IsClosedImmersion.lift z g.imageι (by simpa only [Scheme.Hom.imageι, Scheme.IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι, w] using Scheme.Hom.le_ker_comp h z), where w : h ≫ z = g. The definition lift at ClosedImmersion.lean:210 takes a closed immersion z and an arbitrary morphism g.imageι with z.ker ≤ g.imageι.ker; its body is the ideal-containment construction g.imageι.toImage ≫ IdealSheafData.inclusion H ≫ inv z.toImage. Hom.le_ker_comp at IdealSheaf/Basic.lean:732 supplies z.ker ≤ (h ≫ z).ker; IdealSheafData.ker_subschemeι at IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean:576 and the imageι abbreviation at line 665 identify g.imageι.ker with g.ker. No quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness hypothesis is used. The construction's factorization, if needed downstream, is lift_fac at ClosedImmersion.lean:215. All sources read 2026-10-21.
